relations.quote: A shear of rank $a$ is implemented by $a$ calls of the [address-field interchange](address-interchange.md) procedure.
It is computed by the [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md) of the bit procedure.
The shear is computed with [modular inverses](modular-inverse.md) modulo $q$ of the denominators.
Composition follows the rules of [linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
The shear is counted by the [rational rank](matrix-rank.md) $a$ of $M$, the number of linearly independent rows of $M$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
The shear is used by the [bit procedure](bit-procedure.md), which interchanges two fields.
On every role, the shear is realised as the [endpoint operator](endpoint-operator.md) of the bit network.

symbols.name: radix
symbols.meaning: A fixed odd prime, the radix in which each digit of a field is written.
symbols.quote: Each field is $b$ digits in radix $q$, a fixed odd prime; $b$ and $q$ change meaning here.

symbols.name: digits per field
symbols.meaning: The number of radix-$q$ digits in each field, so it counts digits.
symbols.quote: Each field is $b$ digits in radix $q$, a fixed odd prime; $b$ and $q$ change meaning here.

symbols.name: second matrix
symbols.meaning: Another rational $m\times m$ matrix, whose shear is composed with that of $M$.
symbols.quote: Applying $\Phi_M$ and then $\Phi_{M'}$, for another rational matrix $M'$, adds $M'D$ to $H+MD$, so $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M+M'}$.

symbols.name: chunk digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of digits in a chunk at recursion depth $k$, equal to $m^k$.
symbols.quote: With $e=m^k$ the number of digits in a chunk at depth $k$, $F_k=O(e^\tau)$, so a chunk of $e$ digits is interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time.

symbols.name: time per unit volume
symbols.meaning: The time per unit volume at recursion depth $k$.
symbols.quote: With $F_k$ the time per unit volume at depth $k$, this gives $F_k\le (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.
